issue.title: Monitor diagnostics include the synthetic stage-one failure from test_continuation_baseline
issue.description: tests/monitor/test_continuation_baseline.py::test_run_silent_records_failed_stage_and_preserves_early_exit overrides SASE_ARTIFACTS_DIR but inherits SASE_MONITOR_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR from the outer monitored run. tools/run_silent writes to both stores, so the fixture's intentional exit 7 escapes into the real monitor manifest. Fix the fixture environment boundary and add focused regression coverage proving that an outer diagnostics directory remains untouched. No production pager code is involved.

task_type_fields.impact: Follow-up agents receive fake failures ahead of real diagnostics, wasting limited prompt space and directing investigation toward intentional fixture output.
task_type_fields.repro: Run just check or just check-full via sase monitor on HEAD 2e0dd5ee. Monitor k7zjjhbracj7 emitted a failed stage named stage one with exit 7 and body boom although that test passed. The fixture subprocess inherits SASE_MONITOR_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR and redirects only SASE_ARTIFACTS_DIR.

payload.entry: Related to sase-ee through tools/run_silent diagnostic capture. Typed related link was attempted but blocked by the shared hidden-plans dirty-clone failure tracked as sase-10y.

evidence.note: PROPOSED BY sase-11r.1 (note #1, 2026-09-16, relayed by the sase-11r land agent): that phase's just check-full verify monitor again reported the bogus failed stage 'stage one' / body 'boom' / exit 7 even though the test passed, i.e. the fixture's synthetic failure still escapes into the real enclosing monitor's diagnostics. Rechecked at master c05aa3a94a: tests/monitor/test_continuation_baseline.py:105 still builds env = {**os.environ, 'SASE_ARTIFACTS_DIR': ...} and never overrides or drops SASE_MONITOR_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR, so the leak is unchanged.

Independently reproduced during sase-123.7.6 landing at HEAD 99eb1acc0e: verify monitor g6ee5kawn1cz reported synthetic stage 'stage one' with exit 7 and body 'boom', while the retained just check-full command log contains no such stage and the full pytest lane completed 42,754 tests. The real failures were two unrelated completion-snapshot nodes, confirming the stage-one entry is diagnostic contamination rather than a repository gate.

Independent reproduction during sase-12w.6.3 `just test` monitor tadp9xgwqys8. Selected diagnostics were the synthetic stage named "stage one" with exit 7 and body "boom", while the retained command log's real failures were the 14 sidecar nodes tracked by sase-130 plus tests/completion/test_loader.py::test_fish_loader_sources_grammar_once_and_skips_later_ensure. Confirms the fixture's intentional failure still leaks into the enclosing monitor diagnostics.

Independent reproduction in the ToolRun ledger (athena, 2026-09-24, lead researcher for the sase tool E3/E4 revalidation): the same fixture also inherits SASE_TOOL_RUN_EVENTS (tests/monitor/test_continuation_baseline.py:105 builds env = {**os.environ, 'SASE_ARTIFACTS_DIR': ...}), so tools/run_silent appends its synthetic 'stage one' exit-7 stage into the enclosing sase tool run's stage timeline. Read-only query of ~/.sase/tools/runs.sqlite: 37 of the 101 sase 'check' runs (definition digest 12b1748a5c...) that reached 'test (scoped)' carry nested fixture stage rows; 'stage one' appears in 35 of them; one succeeded run contains a failed stage row. Impact beyond monitor diagnostics: E3 failure triage would read these as real failed stages, so the fix should drop SASE_TOOL_RUN_EVENTS (and SASE_TOOL_RUN_ID) in the fixture as well as SASE_MONITOR_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR; auditing other tests that run tools/run_silent with an inherited env is also worthwhile.

payload.description: Candidate duplicate for nested run_silent stage-event contamination of ToolRun ledger

payload.entry: Fixed under sase-18j.1: tools/run_silent runs its stage command without SASE_TOOL_RUN_EVENTS and SASE_MONITOR_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR (subshell unset), tests/conftest scrubs those plus SASE_TOOL_RUN_ID at session start, and the test_continuation_baseline and test_monitor_diagnostics fixtures (including the run_supervisor path) drop them explicitly. Tests: tests/tool/test_nested_stage_recording.py (nested run_silent records only its own top-level stage; outer monitor diagnostics dir untouched; stages:none run with a pytest child records no stage rows; byte-identical run_silent output without the variables; the real fixture tests leave a poisoned enclosing run untouched).
